resume.short: Data Engineer with 5 years of experience building scalable data pipelines, analytics solutions, and big data platforms. Hands-on with Cloudera on-premises stacks, Azure + Databricks cloud migrations (medallion architecture), and streaming replication from IBM DB2 to Amazon Aurora via Kafka/MSK CDC.
resume.full: Data Engineer with 5 years of experience in building scalable data pipelines, analytics solutions, and big data platforms. Hands-on expertise in designing and maintaining on-premises data pipelines using Cloudera (Hadoop, Hive, Spark), Linux servers (entry points, file watchers, file transfers), and BMC Control-M for orchestration. Re-architecting pipelines from on-premises (Cloudera / SAS) to the cloud using Azure Data Factory for ingestion and Databricks for transformation, applying the medallion architecture. Developing streaming pipelines to replicate transactional data from IBM DB2 to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using Kafka, Amazon MSK, and MSK Connect with CDC. Experienced with CI/CD and DevOps tooling: Git, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Jira, ServiceNow, Docker. Strong skills with Python (10+ years), SQL (5+ years), Shell scripting (5+ years), and Scala (2+ years). Bachelor's degree in Control and Automation / Mechatronics Engineering obtained in August 2018.

hero.title: dadaia-workspace
hero.tagline: Agent-driven SDD ecosystem — spec-driven development with collaborative AI agents.

sections.title: What is it
sections.body: dadaia-workspace is an AI agent ecosystem orchestrated for spec-driven development (SDD). Each agent has a well-defined role and scope — product-engineer, software-engineer, qa-engineer, devops-engineer — and they collaborate through shared specs and contexts.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: Most AI development tools treat agents as generic assistants. dadaia-workspace inverts this: each agent knows its boundaries, reads the specs before acting, and never writes code outside its domain. The result is a reproducible, auditable, and secure workflow.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The operator activates a project context (`dadaia context activate <name>`). Each agent reads the corresponding specs, executes its tasks, and reports back. All agents run on the same LLM but with distinct system prompts and permissions. The project uses Claude (Anthropic) as the base model.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: This portfolio is a React SPA hosted on AWS. The frontend is built with Vite and served via CloudFront with OAC over S3. Infrastructure is managed with Terraform and deployment automated via GitHub Actions with OIDC.

sections.title: Engineering
sections.body: Zero long-lived AWS keys: authentication via OIDC directly from GitHub Actions. Two environments (stage + prod) with identical pipelines. Automated tests with Vitest + RTL + Playwright + LHCI before any deployment.
